strings.name: Amitav Ghosh
strings.summary: Trained in social anthropology, Ghosh traces colonialism, migration and Indian Ocean connections across fiction and nonfiction. The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace and the Ibis trilogy link personal lives to trade and empire. The Great Derangement asks how literature can confront climate crisis, bringing nonhuman life and ecological loss into historical narrative.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Connects colonial history, trade and ecology through the Ibis trilogy and climate writing, widening transnational literary concerns.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Calcutta, India; grew up in India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied in Delhi and completed an Oxford social-anthropology doctoral thesis in 1982.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Indian Ocean historical fiction
strings.highlights.h1.text: The Ibis trilogy connects Asian lives and languages through opium trade and war.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Literature and climate crisis
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Great Derangement examines modern narrative's treatment of climate change and nonhuman agency.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Ghost-Eye appeared in Britain
strings.timeline.t1.text: The novel connects a child’s memories of a previous life with Calcutta, Brooklyn and environmental activism.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published an essay collection
strings.timeline.t2.text: Wild Fictions gathered long-standing reflections on literature, empire, environment and travel.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Received the Jnanpith Award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became the first English-language writer to receive this Indian literary honor.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published The Great Derangement
strings.timeline.t4.text: Examined how climate change challenges modern literary and political imagination.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Launched the Ibis trilogy
strings.timeline.t5.text: Sea of Poppies opened a narrative of colonial trade networks and maritime journeys.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published The Glass Palace
strings.timeline.t6.text: Traced imperial transformation through families in Burma, India and elsewhere.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First novel published
strings.timeline.t7.text: The Circle of Reason began his novelistic exploration of migration and transnational history.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed his doctoral thesis
strings.timeline.t8.text: Submitted Oxford research on kinship, economic and social organization in an Egyptian village.
